svg.title: Ordered fix: try conditionally, release what sorts after the request, refix in canonical order
svg.desc: A thread that already holds watched pages requests page R through a watcher. It first tries a conditional fix; if granted, nothing is released. If the conditional fix fails, every held watched page H is compared with R in the canonical order of group, rank, and VPID. A page that sorts before R stays fixed. A page that sorts after R, or any held page when R's group is still unknown, is fully unfixed with avoid-deallocation registered on its BCB, its watcher cleared, and page_was_unfixed set. R is then fixed unconditionally and the released pages are refixed in sorted order. On success every page is held again in canonical order and page-local observations behind a page_was_unfixed watcher must be re-read; on partial failure the protocol preserves which watchers refixed and which did not. A worked example with header page 0|90, normal page 0|120, and a request for normal page 0|100 in the same group shows the header staying fixed, 0|120 released and refixed, and 0|100 fixed in between.
svg.text: Ordered fix: try conditionally, release what sorts after the request, refix in order
CANONICAL ORDER: group (heap header VPID) → rank: HEAP_HDR before HEAP_NORMAL before HEAP_OVERFLOW → page VPID
Pages with no group sort last. Requesting the group's own header page takes rank HEAP_HDR; every watcher on one page must carry the same rank.
only when other pages are held;
the held set and its order are
H with R in canonical order;
H sorts before R: keep it fixed
H sorts after R, or R's group is still unknown: release H
unfix every fix on H, register avoid-deallocation on its BCB,
clear its watcher, set page_was_unfixed = true
now the request can wait safely:
nothing that sorts after it is held
which watchers refixed and which did
not is preserved; the caller unwinds
EXAMPLE · one heap group whose header page is 0|90
held: header 0|90 (rank HEAP_HDR) and normal page 0|120; request: normal page 0|100 in the same group. Canonical order: 0|90 < 0|100 < 0|120.
So the header stays fixed, 0|120 is released, 0|100 is fixed, then 0|120 is refixed with page_was_unfixed set: its slots and free space must be re-read.
Order comes from the access method's rank and group; the page buffer only enforces it. Restoring a pointer is not revalidation.
